title: He brought an offering.
paragraphs: He brought an offering.
And God said no.

Not because it wasn’t enough…
—but because it wasn’t right.
That’s where we get it twisted.
In Genesis 4, Cain and Abel both came to worship. Both approached God. Both gave.

Same altar.
Same moment.
Different hearts.

Abel brought the firstborn—the best, the costly, the blood.
Cain brought “some” of what he had.

Not first.
Not best.
Just… something.
And that “something” revealed everything.

Because God didn’t reject Cain’s gift.
He rejected Cain’s heart.
“But here’s what we miss…”
Cain wanted God on his terms.

No surrender.
No blood.
No acknowledgment of sin.
Just a transaction.
And heaven doesn’t move for empty religion.

Hebrews 11:4 says Abel offered by faith.
Cain offered by preference.
That’s the difference.

One said, “God, You decide what’s worthy.”
The other said, “God, this should be enough.”

And when God didn’t accept it—
Cain didn’t repent.
He got angry.
Jealous.
Violent.

Sin was already at his door…
but instead of mastering it, he let it master him.

And it led to blood anyway—
not on an altar…
…but on his brother.
Listen.

This is not about farming vs shepherding.
This is not about vegetables vs meat.
This is about a heart that refuses to bow.
Because from the beginning, God was already pointing to one truth:
Without the shedding of blood, there is no forgiveness.
And that blood would not be Abel’s lamb forever.
It would be Jesus.
The Lamb.
The final offering.
The one sacrifice Cain tried to bypass.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because you and I?
We’ve all had “Cain moments.”

Half-hearted worship.
Selective obedience.
Approaching God casually while holding on to sin.
But Jesus didn’t come for perfect offerings.
He came for broken hearts.
Repentant hearts.
Surrendered hearts.
You don’t have to bring “something.”

You come empty—
and receive everything.

Come back to the altar.
But this time… come God’s way.
Through Christ alone.
